Name: Manteigaria (Chiado)
Tips: Standing counter. Watch the natas come out of the oven through the glass. 09:00 breakfast with Fabrica next door.

Name: Convento do Carmo
Tips: 1755 earthquake ruins, nave open to the sky, mummies at the back. Mon-Sat 10:00-19:00 (May-Oct), closed Sundays - fine on Wednesday. 10:00 slot.

Name: Elevador de Santa Justa
Tips: Do not queue or pay - the lift is shut. Best free view of the ironwork and deck is from Largo do Carmo, right where you're standing.

Name: LX Factory
Tips: FALLBACK morning (only if Oceanário is dropped). Industrial complex turned creative hub; shops from ~10:00. Ler Devagar bookshop has the flying bicycle.

Name: Time Out Market Lisboa
Tips: Fallback lunch (no-Oceanário version) before collecting bags for the airport.

Name: Fabrica Coffee Roasters
Tips: Pour-over next door to Manteigaria - the Kenyan V60 + hot nata pairing is famous for a reason.

Name: Oceanário de Lisboa
Cost Range: DROPPED - not visiting. Was 27 EUR/person at the 12:00-15:30 band (13+ pays adult) - 108 EUR for 4
Tips: ❌ DROPPED FROM THE PLAN - decided, not deferred. Never booked, so nothing lost; saves ~108 EUR, and Parque das Nacoes is the opposite direction from everything else on departure day. Replaced by Cristo Rei in the morning and the upper city on foot. Kept here only as a reference pin.

Name: Centro Vasco da Gama
Tips: Fast air-conditioned food court directly opposite Oriente station - the practical post-Oceanário lunch. Oriente is 3 Metro stops from the airport (LIS T1 by ~16:45; TP1038 at 18:55).

Name: Santuário de Cristo Rei
Address: Alto do Pragal, Av. Cristo Rei, 2800-058 Almada
Cost Range: 10 EUR age 13+ / 3 EUR age 8-12 / under 8 free (40 EUR for four)
Tips: 10:00-11:00 THE MORNING STOP on departure day - the Oceanario is dropped. JUST TO SEE IT: lift up, look, come back, 45-60 min is plenty. Opens 10:00 - arrive as it does. GO BY BOLT BOTH WAYS - 09:15 out over the 25 de Abril bridge (~20-25 min, 15-20 EUR), Bolt back at 11:30 to Praca do Principe Real. No ferry and no bus 101 on a departure day: you want a car, not a connection. Order the return from the sanctuary car park, cars are thin up there. Tickets 13+ 10 EUR, 8-12 3 EUR, under 8 free = 40 EUR for four. HARD CUT-OFF: be on a ferry back by 15:00 - this is departure day, TP1038 leaves 18:55 and you want T1 by 16:45. Emergency lane is a Bolt over the bridge to Anjos, ~20 min. Open daily 10:00-19:00, last ascent 18:40.

Name: Praça do Príncipe Real
Tips: 11:45 START OF THE UPPER-CITY WALK on departure day - Bolt drops you here from Cristo Rei, and everything after runs downhill. Garden square under a vast 150-year-old cedar trained flat into a green umbrella you can walk under. Antique shops; Embaixada, a neo-Moorish palace turned shopping gallery, is on the square.

Name: Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara
Address: Rua de São Pedro de Alcântara, 1200-470 Lisboa
Tips: 5 min downhill from Principe Real. Formal terraced belvedere looking straight across the valley at the castle. Busts, a tiled map of the skyline, jacarandas.

Name: Igreja de São Roque
Tips: 3 min from the miradouro. Plain facade hiding the Chapel of St John the Baptist - built in Rome, blessed by the Pope, shipped here in pieces in 1742, once the most expensive chapel in the world. The best free interior in Lisbon.

Name: Livraria Bertrand Chiado
Tips: The worlds oldest operating bookshop (1732), with the certificate on the wall. Next to A Brasileira and the Pessoa statue in Largo do Chiado - the end of the downhill walk before lunch.

Name: Museu do Dinheiro
Tips: RAINY-DAY PICK and FREE. Built inside a deconsecrated church; the basement runs alongside a stretch of the 13th-century city wall found during the dig. Slick and interactive, quick to do. CLOSED SUNDAYS AND MONDAYS.

Name: Nova Pombalina
Tips: CHEAP EATS, 2 min from the Money Museum. Famous for one thing: the sande de leitao - roast suckling pig, crackling, orange-butter bread. Counter service, office workers, no nonsense.

Name: Museu do Aljube
Tips: RAINY-DAY PICK, beside the Se. The Salazar dictatorships political prison, now a museum of censorship, the secret police and the 1974 revolution. The best thing in Lisbon for teenagers who like real history.

Name: Casa-Museu Medeiros e Almeida
Tips: RAINY-DAY PICK and only ~7 min from the apartment. A collectors mansion left as he lived in it - Ming porcelain, Napoleons watch, a room of silver. Almost no visitors.

Name: Museu Calouste Gulbenkian
Tips: RAINY-DAY HEADLINE PICK. One of the great private collections in Europe - Egyptian, Islamic, Persian carpets, a Rembrandt, Monet, and a room of Lalique jewellery. Reopened 2026 after an 18-month renovation. Cafe and gardens: three hours without going outside. WED-MON 10:00-18:00, CLOSED TUESDAYS.
